basis: Carcinoma originates in breast tissue, which has no axis.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder causes hypercalcemia; hypocalciuria is not renal damage. Stones and peptic ulcers occur in under 30%.
Squamous carcinoma originates in salivary glands, included in the gastrointestinal axis.
POMT1 dystroglycanopathies are glycosylation disorders defined by muscular dystrophy and commonly neurodevelopmental impairment; ocular disease varies by subtype.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize partial 1q duplications; other functional organ abnormalities vary with the duplicated segment.
Abnormally mobile or displaced spleen; splenic disorders map to haematologic. Torsion and infarction are potential complications.
Folate metabolic deficiency causes developmental impairment, epilepsy and hypomyelination. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; short bones alone do not establish damage.
Neoplasm originates in the nail matrix.
Defining features include congenital contractures, muscle atrophy, anterior horn degeneration and marked bladder distension; cardiac abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Behavioral and cognitive syndrome caused by bilateral temporal lobe damage; infection is only one possible cause.
Acquired transmissible prion disease directly causes progressive spongiform neurodegeneration.
Gonococcal infection of the endometrium; uterus has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Lymphatic vascular malformation, intestinal malabsorption and ID define syndrome; immune depletion 80-99%. Haematologic lymphopenia and glaucoma (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Combined adrenal steroid synthesis defect; mineralocorticoid excess causes hypertension in approximately 90% of complete deficiency cases.
Localized superficial vascular ectasia with hyperkeratosis affects scrotal skin.
Carcinoma originates in the lung; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease. Metastatic and paraneoplastic conditions are separate diagnoses.
Sarcoma originates in the skin; particular histological subtypes do not define the entire umbrella.
Congenital finger overgrowth with frequent hyperostosis and exostoses; nerve entrapment occurs in under 30%.
Developmental delay and speech apraxia occur in 6/6 patients. Sleep apnea in 2/6 is a separately diagnosed comorbidity.
Hexosaminidase A dysfunction causes GM2 storage and neurodegeneration; damaging ocular disease is not established as common across B1 presentations.
Lewy body deposition and neuronal loss cause progressive dementia and parkinsonism; visual hallucinations do not indicate ocular damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, sometimes with vestibular dysfunction; both belong to the otologic axis.
Peripheral vestibular disorder causes positional vertigo; oscillopsia and imbalance do not establish ocular or central neurologic damage.
Primary mycobacterial infection directly affects the skin; pulmonary disease is not implied.
Autoantibodies disable coagulation factors, causing acquired bleeding disease; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ damage.
